newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-ZANARDI PROVISIONAL POLE FOR CLEVELAND CART RACE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-ZANARDI PROVISIONAL POLE FOR CLEVELAND CART RACE.

text.p: Italian Alessandro Zanardi took the provisional pole for Sunday's Cleveland Grand Prix CART race with a lap more than seven-tenths of a second faster than his closest rival at the Burke Lakefront Airport circuit Friday.

Driving a Reynard Honda, Zanardi, a former Formula One test driver and CART's 1996 Rookie of the Year, turned a lap of 57.423 seconds around the bumpy, 10-turn circuit on the first of two days of qualifying.

"Although the circuit may be better tomorrow -- because there'll be more rubber on the circuit -- we'll be running in hotter weather tomorrow (and slower) so it was important today," said Zanardi, looking for his third pole of the season.
He pointed out that last year his teammate, Jimmy Vasser, won the pole here with his time from Friday.
Even though he was far behind Zanardi in qualifying, American Bryan Herta, who was second fastest in a Reynard Ford, wasn't complaining after struggling in the early part of the season.
"This is a welcome relief from where we've been this year," said Herta. "I'm happy with the car and hope that we can make more improvements."
Michael Andretti, winner of the opening round of the series in Homestead, Florida, was third fastest in a Swift Ford at 58.212 seconds.

Brazil's Gil de Ferran, the race defending champion, was fourth fastest in a Reynard Honda at 58.280. He spun off the course twice trying to keep up with the leaders. "The car was a bit unbalanced...which caused me to have a spin."
If Zanardi holds top place after Saturday's qualifying round it will be his ninth career pole.
Sunday's race, tenth in the 17-race series, will be 90 laps.
